title: All the news from Apple’s HomeView launch event | The Verge
text:
Apple’s October 13th launch event — given the tagline “Welcome Home” — is all about its efforts for the smart home.

The event was headlined by the debut of the HomeView, Apple’s first smart home display. It also launched a collection of smart home devices, including cameras, thermostats, and a smart lock, in partnership with other companies.

On top of the new device categories, Apple also refreshed two familiar ones. The HomePod Mini 2 was announced with support for Siri AI, and the Apple TV 4K also received a Siri AI-focused refresh.

title: Everything Announced At Apple's 'Welcome Home' Event
text:
By Kris Holt Updated: Oct. 13, 2026 10:25 am EST 

Apple

Apple is making a bigger push into the smart home domain. The company invited press and creators to a "Welcome Home" event in New York City on Tuesday to reveal a batch of fresh products, and we'll break it all down for you right here.

Among those was the long-anticipated HomeView — Apple's first smart home hub. In addition, we saw refreshed versions of the Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini. That's not all, because Apple talked up a whole ecosystem of smart home products.

We've had a chance to try Apple's new products. So, be sure to check out our hands-on coverage of the HomeView, Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini 2 for our initial impressions.

Let's dive into everything Apple announced at its Welcome Home event.

## HomeView smart home hub

We've heard rumors for years that Apple was working on an iPad-style display from which you'd be able to manage smart home devices. It was described as the company's answer to Amazon's Echo Show or Google's Nest Hub. Reports suggested it would be called the HomePad, but thankfully Apple steered clear of causing any confusion with the HomePod. Instead, the device is called the HomeView.

The HomeView has a tilting, seven-square-inch Liquid Retina touch display — perhaps paving the way for the touchscreen MacBook that's said to be coming very soon — that's attached to a base with a speaker. There are two variants. You can place one on a table or countertop and mount the other to a wall. 

The display itself has two full-range ... The wall-mounted version doesn't have a base, but Apple says its audio is tuned for wall placement. The screen has a maximum brightness of 500 nits and that can drop down to 0.3 nits (useful if you're using HomeView on a nightstand next to your dozing partner).

The device is powered by Apple Intelligence and has Siri AI baked in. (Reports suggested that Apple had put HomeView on ice until the delayed Siri AI was ready.) You can start a conversation with the assistant on HomeView, and continue on another Apple device. You'll also be able to handoff things like music and recipes from your iPhone to HomeView as well.

HomeView can recognize the face of the person who's interacting with it (up to six people), and automatically switch from a shared household screen to a customized interface for that individual. This should mean the user will have access to their own notifications and calendar, as it can tap into their personal data from their iPhone or iPad. You'll be able to have Apple Watch-style custom "faces" on HomeView that have four adjustable widgets and can feature things like weather details, some favorite photos and Snoopy animations.

...

The HomeView runs on the A18 chipset, the same one that powers the iPhone 16, iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16e and MacBook Neo. It costs a surprisingly reasonable $299 for both the tabletop and wall-mountable versions. The countertop version comes in four relatively muted color options: silver, starlight, rose pink and space gray. The wall-mounted model is available in space gray and silver. Pre-orders open today and it'll ship on November 13. 

HomeView is initially available in English in the US, Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa and the UK. Apple says it'll add Canadian French support later via an update.

## Apple TV 4K (2026)

The newly refreshed Apple TV 4K runs on the A19 chipset, the same one the company used in the iPhone 17 and iPhone 17e. Since Siri AI can pull from personal context on your iPhone, you can ask the assistant to do something like "play that show my sister texted me about" and the Apple TV 4K should fire it up. The assistant may offer suggestions to refine your searches and it can display responses to your questions on screen. Of course, you can control smart home devices using Apple TV 4K as well.

The set-top box has far-field microphones that'll let you talk to Siri AI hands-free. It can pair with up to four HomePod mini 2 speakers for surround sound. You won't have to bother tuning them manually, as the system will automatically calibrate the speakers for your space.

...

Pre-orders for the latest Apple TV 4K open today and it costs $299 ($100 more than the previous model even after a price hike earlier this year). It'll ship on November 13.

...

## HomePod mini 2

Rather than an A-series chip, Apple opted to slot the S10 into the HomePod mini 2. That's the same chipset that the Apple Watch Series 10, Series 11, SE 3 and Watch Ultra 3 run on, and it means you can use Siri AI with the speaker. Apple says that, along with answering questions that spring to your mind, Siri AI can help you get things done, such as adding items to a family calendar. 

However, Apple notes that the latest version of the voice assistant won't be available on the HomePod mini 2 right away. The company will add Siri AI to the device with "a future software update."

The speaker is available in new colors — pink, blue and green to match iMac — as well as white and midnight. The lights on top of the HomePod mini 2 can match the album art of whatever song you're playing at that moment and pulse in time with the beat. Apple calls this feature Sound Glow. What's more, you can use the HomePod mini 2 as a default speaker for your iMac (or two of them for proper stereo sound).

The HomePod mini 2 costs $149. As with the new Apple TV, pre-orders open today. You'll be able to set it up in your home (at least if you're in a region where the original HomePod mini is currently available) starting on October 30.

## Apple Home Collection

Apple has supported an ecosystem of smart home devices for well over a decade through the HomeKit framework, and now it's expanding on that. The company is working with LG and Schneider on devices that fall under an umbrella called Apple Home Collection. The initiative speaks to Apple stamping its own branding more prominently on smart home devices.

The lineup includes indoor and outdoor cameras, a video doorbell, smart door lock, thermostats and temperature sensors. Some will be available in December and others will begin to arrive early next year.

They can all be set up with a tap and managed through the Home app on an iPhone. You'll be able to manage them using Siri and devices like HomeView as well, of course. You'll be able to set up scenes for your smart home devices that can, for instance, change the thermostat, tilt an indoor camera down as you're getting dressed and play music.

All of products support Thread, so they should remain connected if your Wi-Fi network conks out. The devices will also automatically connect to your new Wi-Fi network if, for instance, you change routers or move home. 

Data is encrypted, meaning neither Apple, LG nor Schneider can access it. Apple says you'll need to be running the latest version of iOS to use NFC pairing. It adds that some features require a hub like the Apple HomeView, Apple TV or a HomePod.

title: Top Stories: Apple Product Launches, iOS 27.3 Beta, and More - MacRumors
text:
Apple is still rocking and rolling a week into November, with five new products having launched this week and two more still on tap for next week.

 Things are also moving forward on the software side with Apple releasing the first betas of iOS 27.3 and related updates, bringing a number of tweaks and new features. We're also looking ahead to new products coming in the first half of 2027, so read on below for all of the details on these stories and more!

...

### Apple Launched Five New Products This Week

Apple released five new products on Friday, November 6, following pre-orders that opened last week, including its first touchscreen MacBook Pro models.

 The following new products are now available:

- iPad mini with OLED display and A20 Pro chip
- iMac with M6 chip
- 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip
- 14-inch MacBook Pro with OLED touchscreen
- 16-inch MacBook Pro with OLED touchscreen

Apple's HomeView smart home hub and updated Apple TV 4K box will follow next week on Friday, November 13. 

### Everything New in the iOS 27.3 Beta

Apple this week started testing iOS 27.3, the biggest update to iOS 27 since it launched in September. iOS 27.3 includes some features Apple showed off earlier this year, and it adds all-new capabilities.

 Among the changes in the update are Safari tweaks with a new Vertical Tabs layout option plus an Adaptive Dark Mode feature for websites that don't offer their own dark mode option, Siri AI improvements, an expansion of new iPhone Duo StandBy features to other iPhone models, and more.

The revamped Health app that was in the 27.2 beta for testing but removed prior to the public release has returned in 27.3 and will be seeing a public launch before the end of the year. 

### Apple Alerts Stores to iPhone Duo's Display Cracking Issue

In a memo shared with Apple Stores and Apple Authorized Service Providers last week, and later obtained by MacRumors, Apple provided technicians with guidance on how to diagnose and address the iPhone Duo's inner display cracking issue.

 If a customer reports the issue, Apple advised technicians to inspect the iPhone Duo and repair or replace it in accordance with their standard procedures. While the instructions themselves are straightforward, the fact that Apple issued an internal memo suggests the issue is widespread enough to warrant official guidance.

Meanwhile, Apple CEO John Ternus this week said Apple is not able to predict when it will be able to meet demand for the foldable iPhone, with Bloomberg's Mark Gurman saying that Apple's change from its original plan to launch the device in November in just two countries has contributed to the difficulties in meeting demand. 

### Three New iPads Rumored to Launch in First Half of 2027

The revamped iPad mini launching this week is one piece of Apple's tablet lineup, and Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says the rest of the lineup should be receiving updates in the first half of next year. The iPad Air will reportedly be getting an upgrade to OLED displays, while iPad Pro and base iPad updates should be more modest.

 Before those 2027 updates, there's still some time left in 2026, and while we're not expecting any more major product announcements before the end of the year, plenty of previously announced hardware and software updates are still on their way.

...

App developer Steve Troughton-Smith over the weekend shared a tour of the software on Apple's upcoming HomeView smart home hub. Apple has already demoed the HomeView to selected tech reporters and content creators, but Troughton-Smith offered a closer look at several features, interfaces, and apps.

 CarPlay-enabled audio and video apps from third-party developers will also be supported on HomeView, and Troughton-Smith shared a look at what Spotify will look like on the HomeView as well.

...

The Wall Street Journal's Rolfe Winkler last week reported that flash storage suppliers once "bullied" by Apple have been "getting their revenge" on the company over the past year due to a severe memory chip shortage, which stems from AI companies building out massive data centers that utilize significant amounts of flash storage and RAM.

 As the iPhone took off, Apple became the world's largest buyer of flash storage, and naturally that gave the company a lot of leverage in negotiations.

...

Flash suppliers now have the upper hand, however, and high demand for their chips has resulted in shortages that are expected to persist through 2030 with high prices continuing as a result.

title: Apple Adds Touch and a Glowing Logo to the Mac at Los Angeles 'Pro and Tell' Event | LavX News
text:
John Gruber, who attended Apple's media event in Los Angeles last week, reports new MacBook Pros with touchscreens, tandem OLED PROLED XDR displays and a returning illuminated Apple logo. The event was the second Mac-focused launch of 2026.

Apple Adds Touch and a Glowing Logo to the Mac at Los Angeles 'Pro and Tell' Event

John Gruber attended Apple's media event in Los Angeles last week and reports that the company introduced new MacBook Pros with touchscreens, tandem OLED displays and a returning illuminated Apple logo. The event, called "Pro and Tell," took place at CBS Columbia Square, a building that opened in 1937 as the West Coast headquarters for CBS.

John Ternus, Apple's chief executive, took the stage at 10 a.m. He spoke for a few minutes, recapping recent announcements: the OLED iPad Mini, the M6 MacBook Pro and updates to Creator Studio. He then introduced the new MacBook Pros. "That's why we're here today, to mark another huge moment for MacBook Pro, and for the Mac itself," Ternus said. His announcement that touch was coming to the Mac for the first time drew gasps and cheers.

Touch sits in a secondary role on macOS, Gruber writes. User interface density stays the same with a mouse pointer and changes only slightly to create larger tap targets when a finger touches the screen. Gruber expected this approach and welcomed it. A touch-first redesign of macOS would have damaged the platform, he writes.

The new displays carry the name PROLED XDR. They use tandem OLED panels. Side by side with the previous mini-LED displays, the old screens looked washed. The new ones looked brighter. Apple also compared its panel with a Lenovo Yoga 9 OLED laptop. The Lenovo's colors skewed greenish head-on and turned more green off-angle. Apple's panel held color from any angle. Gruber found Windows 11's handling of HDR images clunky: an HDR image opens in SDR, the display takes five to 10 seconds to "warm up," and the resulting colors look bad.

Weight fell. The 14-inch models lost half a pound. The 16-inch models lost 0.7 pounds. Apple says sustained performance and battery life did not decrease.

The glowing Apple logo returns. The original glow was a byproduct of backlit displays, Gruber notes. OLED pixels light themselves, so Apple engineered a custom light source for the logo without adding thickness to the lid. With the light off, the logo looks like the polished logos on MacBooks since 2016, which helped Apple keep the feature secret during internal testing.

The event format mirrored the MacBook Neo introduction in New York in March. Both featured brief welcoming remarks, a short video and then a hands-on area. Apple did not stream either event online. Gruber argues that Apple should, because the events are good and good things should be shown.

The hands-on area was crowded. Attendees stood shoulder to shoulder in tube-like hallways with black walls. Some tried to swipe the M6 MacBook Pro screens, which lack touch, until someone told them those were the other new models. Gruber compared the scene to the coach cars in Bong Joon-ho's Snowpiercer.

Product briefings followed. Gruber saw a disassembled PROLED XDR panel with five layers, each thin. One writer in another group shattered the front cover glass while passing it around. In Gruber's group, attendees could not touch anything.

The "Pro Workflow Showcase" occupied the third and fourth floors. Demonstrations came from creative professionals. Will and Ed Reid, filmmaking brothers from the U.K., showed "4D Gaussian splatting," capturing immersive 3D scenes with nine iPhones used as synchronized cameras. Jeremy Cowart, a portrait photographer from Nashville, showed a studio workflow that processes hundreds of still photos per minute. Fab Dupont, a record producer who has worked with Bad Bunny and David Crosby, mixed music live in Logic Pro and said he expected to ignore the touchscreen. Susan Fang and Orelio de Jonghe, a design duo, showed 3D-printed clothing and accessories. Azuma Makoto, a Japanese experimental botanist and florist, showed botanical sculptures and machines he uses to control flower blooming; his partner Shiinoki Shunsuke said the team uses analog controls because physical plants demand physical controls. John Knoll, co-creator of Photoshop and an Industrial Light and Magic veteran, demonstrated a miniature LED volume and a motion-tracking camera system he built in his garage, using genlock to sync rendered video with captured video at microsecond precision.

Apple held four major events in 2026. ... The Mac accounts for 7 to 9 percent of Apple's revenue in the second, third and fourth quarters, and 5 to 6 percent in the first quarter. The iPhone accounts for about 50 percent in most quarters and about 60 percent in the first quarter.

title: AAPL Stock Hits Record High As Apple Unveils HomeView, Revamps Smart Home Lineup
text:
Apple (AAPL) shares climbed about 2% to a new record high on Tuesday after the company unveiled several new smart home products at its October 13 "Welcome Home" event, expanding its presence in connected-home devices. 

The announcements included the new HomeView smart display, an updated HomePod mini 2 speaker, a refreshed Apple TV 4K and a range of home accessories developed with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. 

At the time of this writing, AAPL stock was trading 1% higher at around $344.

...

The $299 HomeView marks Apple's entry into dedicated smart home displays, combining entertainment, video calling and household device controls in a single product. Powered by Apple's updated Siri artificial intelligence (AI) assistant, the device can also manage connected accessories such as cameras, doorbells and thermostats. It will become available on November 13. 

Apple also refreshed two existing products after several years without major updates. The $149 HomePod mini 2 is the first update to the speaker since its 2020 introduction, while the new Apple TV 4K marks the first refresh of Apple's TV set-top box since 2022. 

The HomePod mini 2 will become available on October 30, although its new Siri AI capabilities will arrive through a future software update. 

The updated Apple TV 4K will be available on November 13. Apple also announced its Home Collection, developed with LG and Schneider Electric, featuring security cameras, smart locks, video doorbells and thermostats. The accessories will begin rolling out in December.
